claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you're claiming for.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you'd like to claim Child Benefit for? If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to claim for my son Alex. He's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to help me assess your eligibility.

**Is Alex still in full-time education or undertaking an approved training course?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education at the moment. He finished school but hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. I need to check the eligibility rules to make sure I give you accurate information about this situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see from the rules that for a child aged 16 or over, you can normally continue to get Child Benefit if the child is under 20 and in approved education or training. Since Alex has finished school and isn't currently in education or training, I need to understand more about his situation.

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving school?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't done that. He just finished school and hasn't signed up for anything yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask a couple more questions to fully assess Alex's eligibility.

**Are you currently living with Alex in the UK, and are you responsible for him (for example, are you providing him with food, clothes, accommodation, and pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me and I provide for all his needs - his food, clothes, everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful. I have one more important question:

**Has Alex started any paid work since finishing school? If so, is he working 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't started working yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me review the eligibility rules based on what you've told me.

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules I've reviewed:

- Alex is 16 years old and no longer in approved education or training
- He hasn't registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- He hasn't started paid work
- He lives with you and you're providing for all his needs

According to the rules, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training. However, after this 20-week period ends, eligibility would cease unless Alex enters approved education, training, or employment.

**To give you a complete answer, I need to know: When exactly did Alex finish school and leave education?** (This will help determine if the 20-week continuation period is still active or has already ended.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He finished school back in June, so that was about 7 months ago now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to provide you with a clear assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

Unfortunately, **you are not currently eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- Alex is 16 and left full-time education in June (approximately 7 months ago)
- The rules allow for a 20-week continuation period after leaving education, but only if the young person registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services - which Alex hasn't done
- Since Alex finished school over 7 months ago, this 20-week window has passed
- Without being in approved education, training, or a careers service, and without paid employment, Alex no longer meets the eligibility criteria

**However, there may be options going forward:** If Alex were to register with a government-sponsored careers service or enrol in an approved training course, Child Benefit eligibility could be restored. You may want to encourage Alex to explore these options if he's interested in continuing support.

If you have any other questions or if your circumstances change, feel free to ask.
